video.title: I Just Sold a Niche Software Tool for $2.7 Million…Here’s How

summary: Spencer Haws of Niche Pursuits tells how he built and sold Link Whisper, a WordPress internal-linking plugin, for $2.7 million in January 2025. He covers three ways to find software ideas (scratch your own itch, find a gap in big players' features, interview customers), seven marketing strategies, and the broker-led sale process, which was slowed by an SBA loan, a bank switch and a slow buyer's attorney. Key takeaway: a niche plugin with an existing audience, a strong product and affiliate/marketplace distribution reached about $90k/month and an exit via Quiet Light.

tactics.name: Three ways to find software ideas
steps: Scratch your own itch: build a tool for a problem you personally have
Find a gap: look at big software companies and spot features they do poorly or as afterthoughts, then build a dedicated, better version
Interview potential customers (he interviewed many bloggers) to confirm the pain and shape features

quote.text: if you can find, for example, a billion dollar software company that is building all these great features, you might be able to find one of those features that they aren't doing a very good job at.
quote.speaker: Spencer Haws

tactics.name: Seven-channel software growth playbook
steps: Build the best product and keep improving it using customer feedback and competitor monitoring
Content marketing: blog posts, YouTube demos, showing other bloggers using it
Build an email list and run drip campaigns plus regular promotions
Affiliate programme: email buyers an invitation to become affiliates
Outreach to bloggers, YouTubers and SEO influencers with free copies for reviews
Offer a free stripped-down version on WordPress.org as a funnel to paid
List on as many marketplaces as possible

tactics.name: Exit via broker with multiple buyers
steps: Receive inbound acquisition interest and learn the process, even if the deals fall through
List with a broker (Quiet Light Brokerage) in summer 2024
Hold calls and due diligence with many potential buyers
Collect multiple offers and accept the one at full asking price
Expect delays: SBA-financed buyers may take 90+ days, plus bank switches and slow attorneys

lessons.lesson: Solving your own problem gives built-in product insight and conviction for a niche software tool.

quote.text: I truly was solving my own problem when I built Link Whisper.
quote.speaker: Spencer Haws

lessons.lesson: Look for features that large incumbents treat as an afterthought; a dedicated best-in-class tool can win the niche.
Interview potential users before building to validate pain and shape features.
An existing audience and email list is a massive launch advantage ($30k in month one), but it needs ongoing growth channels afterwards.

quote.text: being able to launch that to my existing email list helped a lot.
quote.speaker: Spencer Haws

lessons.lesson: Product quality is the best marketing: great products get talked about and top review lists.
A free version on a marketplace is a strong top-of-funnel for paid upgrades.
Affiliates and influencers with free copies can become a major sales channel, especially in an SEO-review-driven market.
Decline early offers if terms are uncertain; inbound interest teaches you the process and can lead to a better sale with a broker and multiple buyers.
Closing a sale takes far longer than expected; plan for stress and delays from financing and legal counterparties.
